text_read: Whole saved excerpt (copyright page and Part Two section 'Visions & Other Uncanny Phenomena', source lines 1-104).
mode_evidence: A light 'may appear to the mind', listed with a high-pitched sound 'in your ears' and smells, tastes, touches; called 'signs' that the mind is settling. No Pali terms, no parikamma/uggaha/patibhaga scheme, nothing on eyes, 'in front' or visualising. Visions of persons or places are distinguished as arising when the mind is quiet but not established in its object.
onset_evidence: Nothing to induce light; the light arises of itself as a by-product of settling on the breath. Rule of thumb: 'leave them be'; you are not missing anything important by not engaging; engage only under a skilled teacher's personal supervision.

conditions.prerequisites: Supervision by a teacher skilled with such phenomena before engaging them.

stages.label: signs
stages.description: Light, high-pitched sound or other unusual sensation when the mind settles: road signs, not the road.

stages.label: visions
stages.description: Self, another person or place, when the mind is quiet but not established in its object.

what_to_do_with_light: Ignore: do not leave the breath; treat it as a road sign and stay on the road.
obstacles_and_fixes: Visions: breathe deeply into the heart three or four times; if of a person, first spread goodwill.
Sense of having left the body: recall the four properties (breath energy, warmth, coolness, solidity).
External presence: fill the body with awareness and breath energy, then spread goodwill.
cautions: Not everything that arises in a still mind is trustworthy; true information is especially dangerous because it leads you to trust false information.
interpretation: Light is a sign of settling concentration, without value as an object.
practice_summary: Stay with the breath. If, as the mind settles, a light appears, or a high sound, smell, taste or touch, do not leave the breath to follow it; it only shows that you are settling, like a road sign on the way into a city. If a vision of a person or place comes, re-establish mindfulness with three or four deep breaths into the heart (for a person, spread goodwill first). Do not engage these phenomena unless a teacher skilled in them is supervising you personally.

key_passages.locator: Part Two, 'Visions & Other Uncanny Phenomena', 'Signs', source lines 68-74
key_passages.anchor: Sometimes when the mind settles down, a light may appear to the mind
key_passages.paraphrase: A light, a high-pitched sound or other unusual sensation may appear when the mind settles; do not leave the breath; they are signs like road signs.

key_passages.anchor: the general rule of thumb with regard to these things is to leave them be
key_passages.paraphrase: Leave such phenomena alone; engage only under the personal supervision of a skilled teacher; a book can only teach how to pull out of them.

key_passages.anchor: reestablish mindfulness by breathing deeply into the heart three or four times
key_passages.paraphrase: Visions come when the mind is quiet but not established in its object; deep breaths into the heart dispel them.
